sara_w: Customer (acct: acme-inc) reporting intermittent 503s on embeddings calls since ~2026-03-16 14:02 UTC. I grabbed two request ids they saw: 01f8a3b4, 01f8a6d2. Can someone share a tiny curl + Python/JS/Go snippet to hand to the customer and what exact headers/logs we need?

jess_devx: Quick checklist: 1) full response headers (incl x-request-id) 2) SDK name + version (or curl) 3) exact JSON payload 4) region/endpoint 5) timestamps of failures. Also ask them to enable SDK debug logs (REDWOOD_DEBUG=1) if possible. If you have a curl -i or -v paste it here.

sara_w: Pasting the curl -i I ran (redacted key):

```bash
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embedding-1","input":"short text to embed"}'
```

Response headers we observed:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2026 14:04:12 GMT
x-request-id: 01f8a3b4
server: redwood-edge
content-type: application/json
```

Response body: `{"error":"temporary capacity issue"}`

liam_k: Thanks — please ask the customer to re-run with `-v` and to add a client-side timestamp header so we have their clock: `--header 'X-Client-Time: 2026-03-16T14:04:12Z'`. Also ask them to try model `redwood-embedding-1-small` to check if it avoids throttles. Below are compact SDK snippets we can hand them.

Python:
```python
import requests
resp = requests.post(
  "https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/embeddings",
  headers={"Authorization":"Bearer YOUR_KEY","Content-Type":"application/json"},
  json={"model":"redwood-embedding-1","input":"short text to embed"},
  timeout=10,
)
print(resp.status_code, resp.headers.get('x-request-id'))
print(resp.text)
```

Node (fetch):
```js
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-embedding-1', input: 'short text to embed' })
})
console.log(res.status, res.headers.get('x-request-id'))
console.log(await res.text())
```

Go:
```go
package main
import ("bytes" "net/http" "io/ioutil" "fmt")
func main(){
  json := []byte(`{"model":"redwood-embedding-1","input":"short text to embed"}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST","https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/embeddings", bytes.NewBuffer(json))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization","Bearer " + "YOUR_KEY")
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type","application/json")
  client := &http.Client{}
  resp, _ := client.Do(req)
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  b,_ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println(resp.StatusCode, resp.Header.Get("x-request-id"))
  fmt.Println(string(b))
}
```

liam_k: Also have them enable verbose SDK logging: set env `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1` (or `REDWOOD_SDK_LOG_LEVEL=debug` depending on SDK). For curl use `-v` and capture both stdout and stderr. If they can paste the x-request-id(s) + approximate client timestamp we can trace in infra; if it's capacity-related we'll look for model-specific queue spikes and throttles.
